name: Gillis & Persinger 1993: pulsed field, 1 s every 4 s, both sides (20 min)
summary: The intermittent arm of Gillis & Persinger 1993: the lab's burst-firing pattern for 1 s every 4 s along both temporal planes for 20 min, on the same night in three successive weeks. The paper reports no change in this group's aggression score; the rise it reports, and a fall in trust that only approached significance, were in the four people who received the same pattern continuously.
notes: Four people received 20 min of continuous 50 mG fields that simulate the burst-firing of amygdaloid neurons, four received 'this pattern for 1 sec. every 4 sec.' and four were controls, on the same night in each of three weeks, seated in semidarkness in an acoustic chamber (Gillis 1993 pp.1-2 [168-169]). This program plays the 1 s in 4 arm as one rising sweep stretched to 1 s on 3-ms points, then 3 s off: both are this project's reading. Gillis gives no point duration, and the lab's burst file of that period ran at 1-ms points, 275 ms per pass (Richards 1993 p.7 [77]), so 1 s held about 3.7 passes. The paper does not say whether the pause was 3 s or 4 s; where the lab is explicit it is 4 s off (Dixon 2001 p.4 [90]). The point values were never published as numbers (the lab prints the shape only as a small figure). The procedure Gillis cites switched one left-right pair every 0.5 s (Richards 1993 p.3 [73]). Here one left-right pair is on at a time, and the right side is reversed so that the pair's field points through the head. The four sites per side stand for the lab helmet's four solenoids per side on a 7.5 by 5 cm ellipse; the site names are this project's reading. Field: the paper gives 50 mG (5 uT) without saying where it was measured (p.2 [169]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. Support: aggression changed by -0.1 (1.9) in this group, +3.3 (2.3) in controls and +7.4 (3.5) in the continuous group (p.2 [169]; persinger-gillis-1993-continuous-bilateral). Four people per group, one lab, never repeated. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history, implanted devices or pregnancy; stop at once on irritability, fear, headache or distress.
setting: Seated in a comfortable chair in semidarkness in a quiet room, wearing the helmet; the original used an acoustic chamber.
schedule: Three 20-min sessions on the same night in three successive weeks, as in the original. The paper's contrast is with persinger-gillis-1993-continuous-bilateral (read its caution first) and with sham.
source: Gillis & Persinger 1993, Percept Mot Skills 76:168 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8451123/ ; Persinger 1999, Int J Psychophysiol 34:163 (burst-firing 1 s every 4 s, 5 uT) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10576400/ ; Carniello 2020, PhD thesis, Laurentian University, p. 89 (230-point burst-firing file, 3-ms points) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/8c92763c-cd19-4a21-b242-3b572a28ce55 ; Tsang, Koren & Persinger 2009, Electromagn Biol Med 28:365 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20017627/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
